item.title: Jack Bech prepares for emotional game in New Orleans, where his brother was killed
item.description: When the Raiders face the Saints on Sunday in the Superdome, the game will have significant meaning for Las Vegas receiver Jack Bech.
item.content:encoded:
When the Raiders face the Saints on Sunday in the Superdome, the game will have significant meaning for Las Vegas receiver Jack Bech.

Bech's brother, Tiger, was killed in a New Orleans terrorist attack on New Year's Day in 2025, along with 13 others.

“I just want to rewrite this wrong in New Orleans,” Bech told Sam Warren of The Athletic earlier this week. “Get that nasty, dirty taste out of our mouth.”

It will be Jack Bech's first NFL game in New Orleans, the city to which his family would travel to watch Saints games when he and Tiger were growing up.

Jack Bech has been fueled by his brother's memory. And their childhood memories include attending games at the Superdome and dreaming of playing there one day.

Bech said that it "would mean everything" to Tiger to see Jack achieve that dream.

“I know he couldn’t be any happier right now,” Bech said.

A second-round pick of the Raiders in 2025, Bech has caught five passes for 48 yards and a touchdown in two 2026 games. As the Raiders try to move to a surprising 3-0 record (after going 3-14 last year), Jack Bech will be ready to make an impact.

The challenge will be to control and direct the emotions he'll be feeling. Receiver coach Zach Azzani has been helping Bech find the right balance.

“He said, ‘Play the game with emotions; don’t be emotional,’” Bech told Warren. “It’s something that’s been super helpful for me. . . Give it everything, leave everything on that field and see what happens by the end of the game."

Whatever happens, Jack Bech will surely be feeling the presence of his brother in a building where they enjoyed watching Saints games as boys.

item.title: 5 points: The important Cowboys-Ravens storylines
item.description: What storylines will you be following during Sunday’s game?
item.content:encoded:
The Dallas Cowboys head international for the first time in over a decade. Not only is the location different from the last time they traveled abroad, but they also aren’t facing a cupcake team like they did in 2014 with the Jacksonville Jaguars in England.

The Baltimore Ravens may have the same record as the Cowboys, but over two weeks, they’ve proven to be a formidable team that shouldn’t be underestimated. They still have an MVP-level quarterback in Lamar Jackson and a future Hall of Fame running back in Derrick Henry to lead their offense.

From Week 1 to Week 2 the Cowboys defense did improve, but will that improvement be enough to walk out of Rio with a win?

Here are five points to watch for as the game kicks off on Sunday.

First point: (Un)even playing field

Even though the game will count as a home game for the Cowboys, playing internationally will take away their home-field advantage. Despite having a strong contingent of fans in Brazil, it might not be on the same level as a game in Mexico, given its proximity to Dallas.

That keeps things pretty neutral for both teams. The big concern heading into the game, though, is less about the crowd and more about the field conditions. Last week there were reports coming out from players who play soccer on the same field Dallas will be on, talking about how the conditions were less than ideal.

JC Tretter, President of the NFL Players Association, went on Twitter this week to weigh in on their research about the field conditions the Ravens and Cowboys will be playing on.

The uncertainty around what the field will be like when they kick off is probably the biggest storyline, since it could affect both teams. If this game comes down to a missed field goal because a kicker can’t plant their foot right or slips on the field, you’ll be hearing about it all week.

Second point: History in the making

Dak Prescott became the Cowboys franchise leader in passing touchdowns last weekend against the Washington Commanders, passing Tony Romo with 249 touchdowns. Prescott could amass a ton of stats this year that would put him first in many categories on Dallas’s all-time quarterback list.

The one area that’s held him back for so long is postseason success, which will ultimately define his career. The Cowboys were off to a rocky start against the New York Giants, but looked a lot more efficient in Week 2. If Prescott wants this year to be different, the Cowboys have to beat the teams that aren’t the bottom feeders of their division.

Baltimore has issues of their own, but Dallas can’t have a performance against them like they did in 2024, where they beat the Cowboys on the road in a 28-25 victory; that was really 28-6 into the fourth quarter. Prescott shouldn’t take the blame if the defense falls short in this game while the offense performs well, but at the end of the day, he is the leader of the team, so just like postseason success, losing to competitive teams will also define his career if he doesn’t win against teams like the Ravens.

Third point: Start GP up so he don’t ever stop

George Pickens might not be a fan of The Rolling Stones, but “Start Me Up” would be playing in my head all week if I were him. Through two weeks, George Pickens has nine receptions for 68 yards and zero touchdowns. Pickens went over 68 yards receiving last year in 12 games last year.

Not only are thousands of fantasy teams disappointed because they drafted him too high and expected a career breakout season, but he can take this offense to another level if Dallas can find ways to get him going. After Lamb’s performance against the Commanders last week, Pickens might see more one-on-one matchups if the Ravens want to double team Lamb. He may also get more red-zone looks, since both Lamb and Jake Ferguson had two touchdowns each. Kyle Hamilton could find his way to either one of them in that area, opening up the door for Pickens to have a multi-touchdown game if the plan goes that way.

Pickens, like Lamb, has always felt like a momentum wide receiver, and Prescott needs to get him touches early in a game to build confidence. Pickens has been a great teammate this week, saying he’s not concerned about his role in the offense right now and that his presence on the field helps Lamb succeed. All things you want to hear from a player looking for a payday in the offseason. Pickens could be in line for an eight-reception, 100-yard game and two touchdowns.

Fourth point: Under pressure

The Cowboys defense improved marginally last week, but one area still needs a massive upgrade: their pass rush. The Cowboys have allowed a league-high 68.4% completion percentage when generating pressure this season, along with 0.26 EPA per dropback, the second-most in the NFL, per NFL Pro.

The Cowboys have gotten pressure on opposing quarterbacks but haven’t been able to bring them down. They have the fourth-lowest pressure-to-sack rate (7.7%) with just two sacks. Heading into the season, it was unclear who would become the team’s best pass rusher. Dallas threw resources at getting Rashan Gary and Von Miller, along with adding pass rush specialist BT Jordan.

The Cowboys will need to get results when attacking the pocket this week, as Lamar Jackson is the best mobile quarterback they could face all season. Over the past two weeks, Dallas has gotten worse at allowing quarterbacks to scramble out of the pocket. Jackson could win the game with his legs alone on Sunday, which makes it even more important that when the Cowboys get their shot to take him down, they don’t miss.

Fifth point: Ride the rookie wave

In an article earlier in the offseason, I said that if the Cowboys were going to succeed this year, their 2026 class would have to emulate the impact of the 2016 class. Dak Prescott and Ezekiel Elliott were the headliners, but Anthony Brown and Maliek Collins did a lot as rotational players, too.

The Cowboys defensive rookies Caleb Downs, Malachi Lawrence, and Jaishawn Barham have had a good start to their careers through two games. Downs and Barham have been the most active, while Lawrence has improved week to week as he develops his game at the NFL level. He leads all rookies in pass-rush win rate, and while that hasn’t translated to sacks yet, it’s a positive metric in the right direction.

If the Cowboys win on Sunday, all three of their rookie defenders will have to make a big impact and help slow down Derrick Henry at all three levels. If they can do that while also pressuring Jackson in the pocket or forcing turnovers, the main storyline will be whether Dallas’ core defense can carry them for the rest of the season.

item.title: ‘Things I think’ before Giants-Titans: Jameis Winston’s audition, and more
item.description: Sunday’s game could have a big impact on the Giants’ roster, and their seaon.
item.content:encoded:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — I’m sitting in the MetLife Stadium press box more than three hours before kickoff of New York Giants vs. Tennessee Titans. So here is a quick ‘things I think’ before the game.

  1. I have written many times that John Harbaugh raises the floor for the Giants. Based on his track record, 15 winning seasons in 18 years as a head coach and just one season of fewer than eight victories, that should absolutely be the case. Without Jaxson Dart for the rest of the season that theory is about to be tested. If it is correct, this season will not go completely off the rails, no matter who is at quarterback.
  2. There is a lot of chatter that how Jameis Winston plays on Sunday will be a major factor in how aggressive the Giants are in adding a quarterback or two to the roster. I get it, but I am not sure that a one-game test in the rain with steady winds of 24-29 mph and gusts of up to 40 mph, per the National Weather Service, is a fair test. If the Giants don’t trust Winston enough to actually play for an extended stretch, why did they just bestow a two-year, $13 million contract extension upon him.
  3. I’m still not buying the J.J. McCarthy chatter. The Giants had enough reservations about him two years ago to pass on drafting him. Unless Harbaugh’s opinion of McCarthy is vastly different than that of Joe Schoen and the Giants’ scouting department, I can’t see a trade for McCarthy happening.
  4. I still believe the likely path this early in the season is signing a free agent like Jimmy Garoppolo or adding a player off a practice squad. Trades for guys like Gardner Minshew and Justin Fields, both of whom have played for offensive coordinator Matt Nagy, have been speculated about. I would just hope the Giants wouldn’t pay a high price for either.
  5. I have to believe the run-first Giants will carry that to an extreme on Sunday. We should see a lot of heavy formations with Patrick Ricard and Chris Manhertz, and a ton of Cam Skattebo and Najee Harris lugging the rock.
  6. The weather, and probably the opponent, have tickets selling on the secondary market for as little as $10. I will be curious how full the stands are at kickoff.
  7. I will be shocked if Brian Burns (ankle) plays today. The Giants could be without three starters if Burns, Deonte Banks (calf), and Tyler Nubin (calf) don’t play. You may snicker and say “good” when it comes to Nubin, but replacing three starters isn’t simple.
  8. Odell Beckham Jr. played just three snaps against the Los Angeles Rams. If the Giants are run-heavy against the Titans, as expected, I wonder if playing time for Beckham will again be sparse. If things go that way, you have to begin to wonder about Beckham’s place on the roster.
  9. Today might also be a day we find out if Harbaugh has faith in Tyrone Tracy. Considering the elements, does Tracy get some touches?
  10. The Giants have one sack in two games. They better get more than on Sunday against Cam Ward if they are going to win this one.

item.title: Giants' list of QB options to add includes Jimmy Garoppolo, Justin Fields, others: report
item.description: As the Giants get set to host the Tennessee Titans in a rainy, windy game at MetLife Stadium on Sunday afternoon with Jameis Winston as their starting quarterback, they're also contemplating their next move under center.
item.content:encoded:
As the Giants get set to host the Tennessee Titans in a rainy, windy game at MetLife Stadium on Sunday afternoon with Jameis Winston as their starting quarterback, they're also contemplating their next move under center with Jaxson Dart sidelined for the rest of the regular season.

"All options are open," said head coach John Harbaugh.

The list of quarterbacks that New York is interested in includes, free agent Jimmy Garoppolo, Arizona Cardinals backup Gardner Minshew, Minnesota Vikings reserve J.J. McCarthy, San Francisco 49ers backup Mac Jones and Kansas City Chiefs backup Justin Fields, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Earlier in the week, SNY NFL Insider Connor Hughes explored some possibilities that Big Blue might take for a new signal-caller. His list also included Garoppolo, who last played for the Los Angeles Rams in 2024, and McCarthy, who has fallen on the depth chart in Minnesota lately. 

Hughes mentioned that he thought it was unlikely a contending team would trade away their backup quarterback which would eliminate Jones as well as someone like the Cincinnati Bengals' Joe Flacco. 

Whoever the Giants bring in will sit behind Winston to start. New York signed the 32-year-old to a two-year, $13 million extension before the beginning of the season and Harbaugh and OC Matt Nagy are "building the offense around" the veteran.

After a full week of practice, Winston will get his first shot as the Giants starter against the 0-2 Titans. Winston didn't play great after coming in for Dart on Monday against the Rams, going 11-for-27 for 111 yards with an interception in a 28-6 loss. 

Winston, the former No. 1 overall pick in the 2015 NFL Draft, has made 89 career starts and is 36-53. In two starts for the G-Men last season, he went 0-2.

It won't be easy for the veteran on Sunday as inclement weather is in the forecast which could mean both the Giants and Titans keep the ball on the ground for most of the match. As for Winston's backup, the Giants signed Jake Haener to the active roster ahead of the game.

item.title: NFL reportedly requested video of Josh Jacobs incident with running back still on commissioner's exempt list
item.description: A judge denied a motion to permanently seal the video, opening the door for the NFL's request.
item.content:encoded:
Content warning: The following article contains depictions of alleged domestic violence.

The NFL has reportedly filed a Freedom of Information Act request to obtain footage of Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs' alleged assault, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

On Thursday, a judge denied the victim's request to permanently seal the video, opening the door for the NFL to request the footage. That could take weeks, per Rapoport.

From @NFLGameDay Morning: The NFL has officially requested to view the video of the Josh Jacobs incident, while the #Packers RB remains on the exempt list. pic.twitter.com/X9MFHPfXI8

— Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 27, 2026

Jacobs, 28, has been on the commissioner's exempt list since Aug. 30. While on that list, Jacobs is unable to practice or play for the team, though he is still being paid. He's missed the team's first two games of the regular season so far.

With Jacobs unable to play, the running back was able to resolve his legal situation sooner than expected. On Sept. 10, Jacobs pleaded no contest to battery and criminal damage to property. As a result of that plea, Jacobs was also fined $1,000. He was ordered to stay away from the alleged victim and undergo counseling.

With that situation resolved, the door was open for the NFL to hand down an official punishment. That's typically the way the league has operated with its investigations, often waiting until the full legal process plays out before issuing its own punishment.

In this instance, however, the NFL would reportedly like to view footage of the incident before making its call. When Jacobs was arrested in May, reports suggested surveillance footage showed the running back throwing his girlfriend to the ground, then taking her phone.

If the NFL is able to obtain that footage, the league would — presumably — view it and factor that into any possible punishment for Jacobs. It's worth noting, however, that every week Jacobs spends on the commissioner's exempt list counts as time served. Despite not technically being suspended yet, Jacobs has already served two weeks of a potential suspension, should the NFL eventually hand one down.

With its request, the NFL is hoping to avoid another Ray Rice situation. In 2014, Rice was arrested and charged with assault after getting into a physical altercation with his girlfriend.

Rice was initially suspended by the NFL for two games for the incident. Then, video of the assault leaked.

The video, which showed Rice punching his then-girlfriend in the face and dragging her out of a casino elevator, resulted in the NFL suspending Rice indefinitely. The league received heavy criticism for its initial response to Rice's situation, causing commissioner Roger Goodell to eventually admit he "didn't get it right."

That August, Goodell increased future punishments for future domestic-violence situations, announcing players would be subject to a suspension of at least six games for their first offense.

item.title: Fantasy Football Week 3 Start 'Em Sit 'Em: Lineup advice from Justin Boone
item.description: Check out Justin Boone's full list of sits and starts for Week 3.
item.content:encoded:
Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench. 

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 3 rankings. 

Starts

Jared Goff, QB, Lions

vs. Jets

Coming off a four-touchdown effort versus the Bills last Thursday, Goff returns to the fast track at Ford Field for a potential shootout with the Jets. 

The Lions defense has been hit hard by injuries and will force their offense to keep attacking most weeks. That's great news for fantasy managers, since Detroit is loaded with high-quality skill position players who will benefit from inflated stat lines. 

Detroit has the fifth-highest implied point total of the week (27.5) and Goff has traditionally been better at home. He's comfortably inside my top-10 QBs this week. 

Other QBs to start:

  • Kyler Murray at Buccaneers – Murray is out of concussion protocol and facing a Tampa defense that's been struggling so much, they just let Deshaun Watson finish as a top-12 fantasy QB in Week 2.

  • Tyler Shough vs. Raiders – Shough was a top-eight fantasy QB in each of the first two games, in part thanks to Kellen Moore's fast-paced offense. While I'd like to see him not rely as much on fourth-quarter stats, there's no denying his fantasy value at this point. 

Chuba Hubbard, RB, Panthers

at Browns

Hubbard was already looking like one of the best fantasy picks of the year, even before Jonathon Brooks was sent to injured reserve for at least six weeks. Now there's no serious competition for touches — with AJ Dillon serving as the new backup. 

It might seem like we're walking a fine line with Hubbard only getting 13 and 14 touches in the first two weeks, but he's been extremely effective, totaling 151 scrimmage yards, five catches and three touchdowns so far. 

The Panthers offense is humming and another positive game script awaits against a Cleveland defense that's allowed 88 yards to Bhayshul Tuten and 90 yards to Bucky Irving. Hubbard is a high-end RB2 in this matchup who most managers were able to get in the middle rounds. 

Other RBs to start:

  • Breece Hall at Lions – The Lions defense gave up over 100 scrimmage yards to Travis Etienne Jr. and Kendre Miller in Week 1, then let James Cook III post 139 yards last Thursday. Meanwhile, Hall looks healthy and is playing some of his best ball in a while, with 210 yards and a score through two games. 

  • David Montgomery at Colts – Indy's defense has been hemorrhaging fantasy points to running backs, allowing Derrick Henry and Kenneth Walker to top 160 scrimmage yards each. Montgomery may not be on their talent level, but he should have a solid day with the Texans favored on the road.  

  • Quinshon Judkins vs. Panthers – After tough matchups on the road against the Jaguars and Bucs, Judkins gets a Panthers defense permitting the most fantasy points to his position. It's now or never for the second-year back.  

Rashod Bateman, WR, Ravens

at Cowboys

Zay Flowers is trending towards missing another contest due to the hamstring aggravation he suffered in Week 1. Though he traveled with the team to Brazil, it would be surprising if he suited up. Even if Flowers is active, he would likely be on a snap count.

In his absence last week, Bateman led the team with nine targets, which he turned into seven catches, 88 yards and a touchdown. 

We've seen these kinds of spike weeks from Bateman before, only for him to turn back into a fantasy pumpkin, but I'm hopeful he can repeat that success in a game with the highest projected point total of the week at 53.5. 

Other WRs to start:

  • Tee Higgins at Steelers – Higgins has feasted on the Steelers defense during his career, averaging over 70 yards and nearly a TD per game across his last four meetings with them. 

  • Tetairoa McMillan at Browns – With Jalen Coker expcted to play through an ankle injury, McMillan will be the healthiest Panthers wideout on Sunday. Cleveland is allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to receivers through two weeks. 

  • Deebo Samuel Sr. vs. Cardinals – Deebo has nine catches and two carries on the season and is somehow one of the healthier members of the 49ers receiving corps. The 49ers have the third-highest implied point total (28). 

Dalton Schultz, TE, Texans

at Colts

Nico Collins will miss another game with a hamstring injury, putting Schultz in position to lead the Texans in receiving once again. 

Not only did the veteran tight end see a stunning 14 targets in Week 2, he caught 12 of them for 140 yards. There just aren't many tight ends who have that kind of volume in their range of outcomes. 

It also bodes well that the Colts just allowed a 9-101-1 stat line to another slower veteran tight end Travis Kelce. Start Schultz confidently as a top-10 option this week.  

Other TEs to start:

  • Terrance Ferguson at Broncos – Puka Nacua is doubtful to play this week, so Ferguson will have a chance to replicate his 54-yard, one-touchdown effort from last week. Ferguson has scored four touchdowns in his young career and they've all occurred in games where either Nacua or Davante Adams missed. 

  • Mark Andrews at Cowboys – The Ravens have the second-highest implied point total (28.5). Bateman can't catch all the passes and the Cowboys are the seventh-best matchup for fantasy tight ends so far. 

Sits

Bo Nix, QB, Broncos

vs. Rams

It's been a slow start to the season for Nix, who has finished as the QB31 and QB18 in the opening weeks. A date with the Rams doesn't seem like the spot where he'll find his rhythm. 

After stumbling their way through the Australia game and losing Myles Garrett to IR, the Rams defense rebounded in Week 2 with Aaron Donald rejoining the club. 

Even oddsmakers aren't buying into the Broncos this week, making them 1.5-point underdogs at home with an implied point total of 21. 

Other QBs to sit:

  • Matthew Stafford at Broncos – Stafford had a terrible outing versus the 49ers and a great showing against the Giants. Unfortunately for him, the Broncos defense carries a degree of difficulty much closer to the Niners matchup. Puka Nacua will be missed in this contest if he can't go. 

  • Baker Mayfield vs. Vikings – The Buccaneers offense is discombobulated at the moment, so much so that Baker wasn't even able to capitalize on a revenge game versus the Browns last week. Facing Brian Flores' Vikings defense is the opposite of a get-right spot. 

TreVeyon Henderson/Rhamondre Stevenson, RB, Patriots

at Jaguars

After being one of the toughest matchups for fantasy running backs last year, the Jaguars have picked up where they left off by holding every back they've encountered so far to less than 40 rushing yards. 

Though Stevenson's fumbling issues popped back up last week and led to an increased workload for Henderson, we'll likely see this remain a fairly even split. So don't expect volume to save the day for either of these backs. 

Henderson's explosiveness gives him a chance to hit one big play at any time, like we saw last week on his 39-yard TD run. However, plays like that are extremely rare against Jacksonville's front. 

Other RBs to sit:

  • Travis Etienne Jr. vs. Raiders – Etienne's usage has been puzzling, being stuck in a three-man committee each of the first two games. He was also limited in practice for part of the week with a hamstring injury. If you're starting him, you have to understand the risks by now. 

  • J.K. Dobbins vs. Rams – Despite an injury scare last week, Dobbins somehow emerged as the healthiest Broncos runner. RJ Harvey is also expected back from his hamstring injury for this game, while rookie Jonah Coleman landed on IR with ankle issue. Even so, Dobbins has only managed 36 rushing yards in each of the first two outings, with no targets and no touchdowns. 

  • Jacory Croskey-Merritt vs. Seahawks – The Commanders just lost the engine of their offense in Jayden Daniels and now have to take on the ferocious Seahawks defense. JCM hasn't looked bad as the lead back this year, but this isn't the spot to play him for fantasy. 

Stefon Diggs/Terry McLaurin, WR, Commanders

vs. Seahawks

Speaking of the Commanders, we have to downgrade their entire offense this week. Even though Marcus Mariota can give them 60-70% of what Jayden Daniels did, the loss of their franchise quarterback completely changes how defenses prepare for this attack. 

While they might eventually settle in with Mariota under center, that's not going to happen this week against a Seahawks defense that's allowing the fewest fantasy points to receivers. 

Diggs will be startable in other weeks, but he's a risky TD-or-bust flex option in this contest. McLaurin's outlook is even murkier after he struggled last season when Daniels was out of the lineup. 

Other WRs to sit:

  • Luther Burden III/Rome Odunze vs. Eagles – Few teams can support multiple fantasy players when they're starting their second- or third-string quarterback. However, Burden and Odunze weren't putting up big numbers even when Caleb Williams was playing. Don't panic sell; just send them to your bench until Caleb returns, which looks like it will be in 3-4 weeks.

  • Courtland Sutton vs. Rams – Sutton has posted two catches for 11 yards in the opener and three grabs for 25 yards in Week 2. Now he gets the Rams and 49ers over the next two games. Despite being 79% rostered in Yahoo leagues, you can drop him without hesitation. 

  • Brian Thomas Jr. vs. Patriots – Thomas hasn't topped 40 yards in a game this season and the Patriots have held every receiver they've faced aside from Jaxon Smith-Njigba to 35 scoreless yards or less. BTJ is a boom-or-bust WR4/flex who's unlikely to boom versus New England.   

Colston Loveland, TE, Bears

vs. Eagles

It doesn't matter where you drafted him; you can't play Loveland right now. After giving you zero fantasy points in the opener, he managed just one catch for three yards in a rain-soaked loss to the Vikings. 

It's shocking results for a player who was a target hog down the stretch and into the playoffs last year, but it's the current reality. The situation is only made worse with Case Keenum set to start if Tyson Bagent isn’t ready to go coming off a concussion.

On top of it all, the Eagles have allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to tight ends, holding everyone at the position to 16 yards or less. Send Loveland to the bench and we'll reassess in better matchups when Caleb Williams is healthy. 

Other TEs to sit:

  • Harold Fannin Jr. vs. Panthers – Fannin got more involved in a good matchup with the Bucs last week, but the Panthers have been much tougher on tight ends this year. With Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion providing real target competition, Fannin is more of a TE2 streamer. 

  • Brenton Strange vs. Patriots – New England was the sixth-hardest matchup for tight ends last year and has carried that over as the fourth-worst opponent for the position this season. Meanwhile, Strange has been held to 23 yards and 17 yards in his first two outings.

item.description: A one dimensional offense, and a defense that couldn’t get stops gives WVU fans a reality check.
item.content:encoded:
Their Defense was significantly better than ours

Neither the Oklahoma State or WVU defense is going to want to watch film from this game, but in the 2nd half the OKST defense got some key stops when it had to. After getting an interception on the first drive of the 2nd half here is what the next 4 OKST offensive possessions produced: Touchdown, Touchdown, Field Goal, Touchdown.

Game over.

In all OKST racked up 609 yards of total offense, and averaged 14.4 yards per pass attempt. What surprised me the most was the success that OKST had running the ball. They carried it for 220 yards and averaged 5.4 yards per carry.

To me it looked like our defensive game plan was to not pressure the QB or load up the box against the run. We had 4 safeties on the field which is not something we have done in other games this year. Saying it didn’t work is the understatement of the century. The OKST quarterback was only truly under pressure on 1 drop back and OKST was more than happy to run the ball for 5 yards per play.

Their Offense was more balanced

When you look at our offensive stats you would expect these to be part of a WVU win:

  • 29 first downs
  • 9/17 on 3rd down
  • 335 rushing yards

But then you get to the passing yards:

  • 10/22 132 yards and 1 interception

Those rushing stats will be enough to win some games in the Big 12, but not this one. In the 2nd half the OKST defensive line started making running the ball much more difficult and WVU did not have an answer. Michael Hawkins was sacked 4 times all of which were on key 3rd or 4th downs. The passing game never had the chunk plays that we were seeing in the previous 3 games.

Meanwhile OKST could do whatever it wanted pretty much the entire game. We held them to 2 field goals and got one interception in the red zone, or this game would have been ugly very early.

Key Moment

In the 2nd quarter we were up 14 – 6 and were asserting our will on offense. The previous drive was a 16 play 75 yard touchdown drive and this one was going to exact some way. On a 3rd down in the red zone with a chance to go up 21 – 6 Michael Hawkins rolled to his right and threw towards the end zone. An OKST defender made a great play by deflecting the ball and it went right into the hands of a different OKST defender. OKST would score a touchdown on that possession to bring it to 13 – 14 at the half.

It felt like were dominating the game at that point. They were settling for field goals and we were running the ball down their throats. For a visiting team to go down 21 – 6 would have been a completely different mindset for them going into halftime than the 14 – 13 score. We had a chance to step on their throats early and we didn’t.

item.title: Jets vs. Lions: Best odds, bets, and parlays
item.description: New York Jets vs. Detroit Lions Week 3 best player prop bets and parlays
item.content:encoded:
After a long wait following their “Thursday Night Football” loss, the Detroit Lions come home to Ford Field to host the New York Jets. Former defensive coordinator and now head coach Aaron Glenn arrives after an overtime loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 2. Both teams want to get the bad taste of last week out of their mouths.

Last week I went 1-2 again, and wide receiver Jameson Williams was two catches away from hitting that bet. This week I am starting something a bit different: odds for just the bold bet, plus the parlay odds if you combine everything.

Here are three wagers to watch on Sunday afternoon. The odds are with FanDuel Sportsbook.

1. Lions -6.5 spread (-115)

Of all the bets here, this is the simplest. The Lions are favorites to win, and the spread is set at 6.5, which seems about right for this matchup. Detroit is at home, coming off a bad loss, and the team plays better after a loss. They also have extra rest, with their Week 2 game on Thursday, while the Jets are on the road after an overtime loss.

Detroit’s secondary has been rough through two games so far, but this week is their chance to rebound. The Jets are down a tight end in Mason Taylor, and starting wide receiver Adonai Mitchell is currently in a cast dealing with a finger injury. With the Jets’ main targets in the passing game being wide receiver Garrett Wilson and tight end Kenyon Sadiq, I think Detroit will take advantage and keep the offense in check.

Detroit’s offense is tough to contain, averaging 31 points a game so far this season, and I think they’ll put up roughly the same number again this week. With the Lions’ offense tough to slow down and the Jets’ passing attack lacking weapons due to injury, Detroit gets too big a lead for New York to come back from and covers.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.70

2. Jared Goff Over 258.5 passing yards(-113)

Despite the Jets allowing the second-fewest passing yards in the league (285 total), they haven’t faced an offense like Detroit’s. The Titans offense is still young and working through things, and the Packers are dealing with injuries. The Lions offense is mostly healthy and, despite having a new offensive coordinator in Drew Petzing, has a dangerous passing attack. Wide receivers like Amon-Ra St. Brown, Williams, and Isaac TeSlaa, along with tight end Sam LaPorta and running back Jahmyr Gibbs—that’s a lot to worry about for a defense.

The Jets were the first team in NFL history last season not to record an interception, and part of that was a lack of skill in the secondary. They traded away their star cornerback Ahmad “Sauce” Gardner in 2025, and even though they’ve added safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, he’s still on the sideline with an injury. Goff threw for over 300 yards against the Bills, granted they were playing from behind the entire game, but the Bills defense isn’t a slouch either. I believe Goff will beat this line and have a day against this Jets secondary.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.85

3. Jahmyr Gibbs over 89.5 rushing yards (-113)

Again, the Jets defense is their strength, but while the passing game will be working for Detroit, it’ll open up the running game. While Gibbs only ran for 52 yards against Buffalo, again mostly because the team was down by so much early, the opposite will be the reason why this week. The Lions offense also struggled last week with starting left guard Christian Mahogany and right tackle Blake Miller out due to injuries. They both return this week, leaving center Juice Scruggs as the only backup lineman playing.

New York also hasn’t seen a running back like Gibbs so far this season. The Tennessee Titans’ best running back is Tony Pollard, and without Josh Jacobs, the Packers had MarShawn Lloyd as their top option. Neither of those players comes even close to what Gibbs is, not just as a running back but as a receiver. Gibbs has been the lifeblood of the offense so far this season, and Detroit will continue to make sure he’s the focal point and run him over 20 times a game.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.85

If you want to turn these three single bets into a same-game parlay, the odds are +504 and $10 -> $50.50

Record: 2-4

Brandon’s Bold Bet

If you want to go bold and build a big parlay that could pay well, put these three bets together in a parlay:

  1. Jameson Williams anytime touchdown (+160)
  2. Sam LaPorta 5+ catches (-118)
  3. Jared Goff 2+ passing touchdowns (-198)

While he hasn’t found the end zone yet this season, I think Williams is due to find it this week against the Jets secondary. He’s had a slow start to the season, struggling with drops in Week 1, and only getting two catches in Week 2. It’s tough to contain Williams for so long; eventually he’s going to break one loose, and Goff has had chances to throw to him, but Williams has either dropped it, or Goff couldn’t get the play off in time.

Speaking of Goff, he’s averaging three touchdown passes a game this season, so for him to only throw two seems simple. The Jets defense has allowed three passing touchdowns so far, so while it’s been difficult for opposing quarterbacks to find the end zone, as I mentioned earlier, there’s too much firepower in this offense to be contained, and I think Detroit’s offense has a day.

Goff has also been loving having LaPorta back in the lineup, catching 11 passes for 100 yards and a touchdown. He’s averaging 5.5 catches a game, so for him to meet his average seems doable. The Jets linebackers led by DeMario Davis won’t make things easy for him, but as a friendly checkdown for Goff, he can get five catches with ease, I believe.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $43.59

Record: 0-2

Do-it-all parlay

If you want to combine all six plays into a parlay and go big or go home, here are the odds:

  1. Lions spread
  2. Jared Goff over 258.5 passing yards
  3. Jahmyr Gibbs over 89.5 rushing yards
  4. Jameson Williams anytime touchdown
  5. Sam LaPorta 5+ catches
  6. Jared Goff 2+ passing touchdowns

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $259.04

Record: 0-2

Use this information however you like. You can ignore it and watch the game, or, if you want to risk some money, follow these recommendations or test your own luck. Whatever you decide, please gamble responsibly and bet only money you can afford to lose.

item.title: Trent McDuffie, Patrick Surtain headline Sunday Night Football matchup
item.description: Trent McDuffie and Patrick Surtain II are must-see TV
item.content:encoded:
Trent McDuffie of the Los Angeles Rams and Patrick Surtain II of the Denver Broncos will have the rare opportunity on Sunday Night Football this week: They’ll put more star power in the cornerback matchup than in the game’s quarterback matchup.

Of course, cornerbacks from different teams aren’t on the field at the same time, just like opposing quarterbacks aren’t. And it’s not like Matthew Stafford and Bo Nix are lacking for attention, popularity and a spot in the public consciousness.

But both the Rams and Broncos will have one of the best cornerbacks in the sport on the field for their respective defenses on Sunday, which should be a treat for fans who appreciate defensive excellence.

McDuffie has been excellent since breaking into the NFL with the Kansas City Chiefs in 2022, immediately claiming a starting role for Steve Spagnuolo’s defense as a rookie and helping lead that franchise to a Super Bowl title. He earned All-Pro honors each of the next two seasons and was a key part of another Super Bowl win in 2023, too. It was clear from the jump that this was a player with a rare combination of coverage skills, physicality and legitimate boundary to slot versatility.

His tremendous play has continued into his first season with the Rams. Through two games, McDuffie has been targeted nine times and only allowed two receptions while breaking up an NFL-best six passes.

Then there’s Surtain, a preordained superstar since his well-known last name popped up in the high school/college football recruiting world. His dad was a stellar cornerback in his own right, spending 11 years in the NFL with the Chiefs and Miami Dolphins, twice earning All-Pro honors and three times receiving a Pro Bowl nod.

The younger Surtain has taken the family pedigree to another level. He’s just the third cornerback in the last three decades to win AP Defensive Player of the Year, he’s already been an All-Pro three times (twice on the first team) and he’s firmly established himself as one of the best defensive players in the sport regardless of position.

Both of these cornerbacks are stars. They’re not unstoppable, though, and while it may be extremely difficult to challenge them, it should make for some fun game plans from Sean McVay/Nathan Scheelhaase and Sean Payton/Davis Webb to try to trip them up even a time or two in this matchup.

A quick, personal note on how exciting it is to have these two young studs both in action in tonight’s high-profile matchup: While driving to a college football broadcast (my real-world job) on Saturday, I was talking to my broadcast partner about NFL cornerback play. He was a multi-time Division II All-American at cornerback, graduated with an NCAA record for pass breakups in a career and had a brief stint in an NFL training camp. The guy knows the position.

The first two guys he said he loves to watch at cornerback today? Trent McDuffie and Patrick Surtain II.

He’s going to have fun watching those two do their thing on Sunday night. I have a feeling that will be a treat for everyone watching.

item.title: Through two weeks, several seats are heating up
item.description: 10 of 32 jobs opened after 2025. Surely, more will be vacant in January.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL means plenty of things, from No Fun League to Not For Long. That's never been more true for coaches.

Last year, 10 of 32 jobs became open. Whatever the number this time around, the number will be closer to nine than none.

Through two weeks, more than a few seats are getting hot. Or, as the case may be, hotter.

We'll start with Colts coach Shane Steichen, mainly because of what team owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon said after the 2025 season ended: "We have been very clear with [G.M.] Chris [Ballard] and Shane that giving them another opportunity means that the sense of urgency for them to deliver and perform has never been higher."

So far, the Colts are winless. The defense has given up more than 500 yards in each of the first two games. Obviously, something needs to change or there will be a housecleaning in Indianapolis.

Next on the list is Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles. Since starting 2025 with a 6-2 record, the Buccaneers are 2-11. Imagine the angst in the Glazer suite last week while they had to sit there and wait two hours for the likely loss to the lowly Browns to become official. A turnaround is a must.

Jets coach Aaron Glenn wasn't one-and-done after 2025, in part due to a buyout that would have exceeded $40 million. The season started with a suffocation of the Titans and former Jets coach Robert Saleh. In Week 2, a blown 10-point lead, widely-criticized late-game clock management, and a decision to receive the opening kickoff of overtime have increased the pressure on Glenn to do more this year than he did last year.

Things are looking grim for Dan Quinn in D.C. For some, it's already become a given that Quinn will be gone after his third season — especially if it's another 5-12 showing, or worse. The latest Jayden Daniels dislocated left elbow likely won't buy Quinn a mulligan.

Packers coach Matt LaFleur is facing an uprising in the land of beef and cheese. Yes, he got an extension after the 2025 season. But he wouldn't be the first coach who received a new contract one offseason and a pink slip the next.

Lastly, we'll mention Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh. He made the playoffs in each of his first two years on the job. This year, however, has started in disastrous fashion. He has two years left on his five-year, $80 million contract after 2026; the buyout could buy him one more year. It all comes down to whether the Chargers play dramatically better than they did against two teams that combined in 2025 for a record of 6-28.

Any, some, or all of the coaches listed above could turn things around. After all, 15 games remain. And other coaches who are currently safe could end up in hot water as the season unfolds.

Either way, it makes sense to be watching the situation closely, because the NFL head-coaching industry has proven to be a high-turnover business. And, as former Cardinals coach Jonathan Gannon acknowledged once it became clear he was on the hot seat in 2025, it's the business they've chosen.

item.title: Brock Bowers injury update: Raiders tight end reportedly expected to make season debut in Week 3 against Saints
item.description: Bowers had knee surgery shortly before the start of the season.
item.content:encoded:
Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers is expected to play against the New Orleans Saints in Week 3, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported.

The week had appeared to be trending in a positive direction for Bowers, who underwent a surprising knee surgery ahead of Week 1. After logging limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday, Bowers got a planned rest day, per head coach Klint Kubiak.

The team also did not elevate TE Chris Myarick from the practice squad, as they had in each of the past two weeks with Bowers inactive — a possible indicator of Bowers' availability.

The No. 13 pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, Bowers quickly developed into one of the league's top tight ends. He had 112 catches for 1,194 yards and five touchdowns as a rookie. Last season, he still had a team-high 64 receptions and seven touchdowns, despite missing five games because of injuries.

Bowers underwent a meniscus trim just days before the start of the season after his knee bothered him during training camp. He's so far missed the Raiders' first two games with Michael Mayer starting in his place.

item.title: Chiefs-Dolphins Week 3 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride
item.description: Putting our predictions on the record before Kansas City’s Sunday afternoon road battle in Miami.
item.content:encoded:
It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Miami Dolphins, our writers predicted the final score and result.

The Chiefs return to Hard Rock Stadium — where they won Super Bowl LIV in February of 2020 — as 10.5-point road favorites according to FanDuel Sportsbook. This line reflects the Kansas City offense’s potent start to their 2-0 campaign paired with the Dolphins losing their first two contests by a combined score of 62-26.

This will be the first meeting between the teams since the Chiefs came out on top of a bitterly cold AFC Wild Card matchup in Kansas City in January of 2024.

We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction!

Jared Sapp (@TrumanChief)

Many will expect a Kansas City blowout this week against possibly the league’s worst team. The Chiefs team we have seen through two weeks easily could put over 50 points on the Dolphins. But I don’t expect Kansas City to pursue that.

On what will be a hot afternoon in South Florida, Chiefs will likely prioritize a moving clock to shorten the game ahead of what suddenly shapes up as a very important meeting with the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4. I’m predicting a comfortable Chiefs win in a game that will never be in doubt. But I don’t think there will be enough possessions for Patrick Mahomes and company to go truly crazy. I can see a garbage time Dolphins score making the game look more respectable than it truly was.

Chiefs 27, Dolphins 16

Caleb James (@CJScoobs)

The Chief should never overlook an opponent, but this week they need to be thinking big picture against a struggling Miami team that looks more concerned with draft status in April than winning games right now.

The Dolphins rank dead last in sacks allowed with 9 given up on the season, and rank dead last in sacks with zero through two games.

After being blown out in back-to-back weeks by the Raiders and 49ers, they do not appear to be a team capable of making the playoffs, and one that is looking to transition under first-year head coach Jeff Hafley.

If the Chiefs are wise, they will look to put their foot on the gas early and try to get their younger players reps while building in rest for key players like Chris Jones, Travis Kelce, and Kenneth Walker ahead of a critical AFC West showdown against the Raiders next week.

Chiefs 35, Dolphins 13

Mark Gunnels (@MarkAGunnels)

I just don’t think Miami has enough to hang with Kansas City for four quarters. The Chiefs are going to control this game on the ground with Kenneth Walker, which is only going to make life easier for Mahomes and open everything else up. Defensively, I trust KC to make Miami one-dimensional and force them into mistakes. I got the Chiefs winning this one pretty comfortably.

Chiefs 38, Dolphins 10

Maurice Elston (@MrMauriceElston)

On paper, this should be a blowout. The Chiefs are 2-0, the Dolphins are 0-2, and Kansas City is the better team across the board. The biggest danger is letting Miami hang around. The Chiefs have a habit of playing down to their competition when they could put their foot on the gas. Hopefully, Eric Bieniemy’s fire and emphasis on discipline help them avoid that trap.

Miami’s clearest path to making this competitive runs through De’Von Achane. If the Chiefs slow him down, I don’t see the Dolphins keeping pace. Kansas City should be able to take control early and rest its starters in the fourth quarter.

Chiefs 30, Dolphins 13.

Matt Stagner (@stagdsp)

Two teams cross paths on Sunday with very different trajectories. The 0-2 Miami Dolphins look to be in a rebuild year. There are some pieces in place that remind fans of what they could have been– a dangerous team built on speed. But the current struggles seem to go back to the trenches, where they don’t have a great pass rush or offensive line. The Chiefs are two games into the Kenneth Walker/Emmett Johnson era on offense, and they’re unlikely to slow down this week. Watch how fast Spagnuolo’s defense looks with Delane back on the field. The Chiefs should win comfortably, and their ability to not let teams like this hang around is an important step.

Chiefs 38, Dolphins 17

Dakota Watson (@D_Watson56)

I don’t foresee a trap game for the Chiefs this Sunday. While the score may be closer than most fans think it should be, it will only be because Andy Reid doesn’t like to embarrass other teams with a blowout.

I think the Chiefs’ offense will remain balanced. I expect to see more Emmett Johnson in the rotation as they try to reduce the wear and tear on Kenneth Walker early in the season. The defense will feast with at least two takeaways.

Chiefs 30, Dolphins 14

Rocky Magana (@RockyMagana)

Listen, let’s be real. The Miami Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL, and it’s not close. Their only player on offense who is worth his salt is De’Von Achane, and teams are just stacking the box to shut him down. Malik Willis is not an NFL starter, and on defense, they’ve recorded zero sacks so far this season. If you’re looking for a silver lining for this Miami team, it’s that, for a bad team, they have protected the football and are +1 in the turnover department. Still, this is the NFL, and if you don’t show up, you’re going to lose.

That being said, I think we’re still early enough in the season that the Chiefs still have a bad taste in their mouths. If you wanted to get Emmett Johnson some touches under his belt, this is the game to do it and give Kenneth Walker a chance to rest his legs. At the end of the day, the Chiefs should control this game and win by at least two scores.

Chiefs 30, Dolphins 9

Nate Christensen

Miami has been a rough team through two weeks, which is by design. Their dead cap is more than what they’re paying their roster this season. They don’t have much talent on either side of the ball. This should be an easy game for the Chiefs and hopefully an opportunity to get some other guys in the game and get reps.

Chiefs 30, Dolphins 10

Ron Kopp Jr. (@RonOnChiefs)

This game really should look like a matchup between a veteran, contending team and arguably the worst roster in the NFL. The Dolphins are made up almost entirely of rookies on the defensive side of the ball. That should be music to the ears of quarterback Patrick Mahomes and an offense that seems to be clicking on all cylinders.

I’m expecting Kansas City to continue producing explosive plays and build an early lead. With the defense playing in the lead, we’ll see the pass rush and pass coverage pop once again.

item.title: Miami Dolphins offensive line review: Tracking the guards in Week 2
item.description: A weekly scorecard tracking the development of Dolphin guards Kadyn Proctor and Jonah Savaiinaea.
item.content:encoded:
While rebuilds are built in the trenches, progress can be difficult to spot from week to week. Each week, the Miami Dolphins Guard Tracker will follow the development of Kadyn Proctor and Jonah Savaiinaea, two young guards Miami hopes will anchor its offensive line for years to come. Along with PFF grades, penalties and snap counts, we’ll incorporate evaluations from Dolphins film analyst Coach Eric Smith (@OLCoachSmith63) to provide additional context. This inaugural post will cover the first two weeks.

Kadyn Proctor

Coach Smith’s Takeaways

  • Proctor is not getting physically overwhelmed. 
  • He’s making assignment, leverage and processing mistakes, but he often corrects mistakes quickly. 
  • There are numerous examples where a small technical adjustment turns a bad rep into a potentially explosive play.

Jonah Savaiinaea

Coach Smith’s Takeaway

  • Savaiinaea’s play is consistent and assignment-correct. He rarely receives negative marks.
  • He doesn’t produce many highlights, but he doesn’t produce many disasters either.
  • In both videos, Smith basically describes Savaiinaea as the offensive line equivalent of a cornerback nobody notices because quarterbacks never throw at him.
     

What We Learned

Through two games, Proctor and Savaiinaea appear to be taking different developmental paths. Proctor has flashed the physical traits that made him a first-round pick but continues to work through the technical challenges that come with learning a new position. Savaiinaea, meanwhile, has quietly become one of the most consistently graded linemen on the roster according to Smith’s evaluations – which is a curious departure from PFF’s grades. The sample size remains small, but both young guards have played 100% of the Dolphins’ offensive snaps through two weeks, giving Miami plenty of film to evaluate as the rebuild continues.

 
While I’m not overly familiar with his insights, I’m highly impressed with Coach Eric Smith’s analysis. You can check out his work at https://www.youtube.com/@OLCoachSmith63 and https://x.com/OLCoachSmith63.

item.title: Arizona Cardinals fans are already abandoning the bandwagon
item.description: Cardinals fans don’t see things getting better against the Niners.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Cardinals fans and fans across the country.

One week makes all the difference.

The Cardinals were a meager 4.5-point underdogs, they had people starting to believe and then it went sideways, and now the Cardinals are back to 8.5-point underdogs ahead of the matchup with the Niners according to FanDuel Sportsbook.

Last week on game day, we saw the belief in the direction of the Arizona Cardinals soaring, as 85% of fans thought they were heading in the right direction, with a majority excited about the defensive performance against the Chargers.

Then, reality comes crashing down, you have the worst offensive performance in a decade (when the starters are healthy) and the defense plays valiantly but still gets beat up by a backup quarterback.

So, now we see the doubt starting to creep in as the belief in the direction of the team is down big time.

A nearly 30% drop because they lost to maybe the best team in the NFL, means fans are wanting the turnaround to be swift and that they thought it was close after week one.

I think part of the non-belief stems from fans are not confident heading into this one. As an astonishing 64% don’t think the Cardinals will be competitive in this one.

Let’s hope the 36% are right.

Action report from the bookmakers

Los Angeles Chargers at Buffalo Bills

Joey Feazel, head NFL trader at Caesars Sportsbook: "Tale of two teams. The Bills have been very impressive and Josh Allen is making separation in the MVP market early on, which isn't something you usually see. Chargers have a tough schedule upcoming and blew the first two games agains teams they were expected to beat. As expected, we're seeing mostly Bills action and I don't see that changing. Lookahead was Bills -4.5, we're up to a juiced 7. I wouldn't be surprised if we get to 7.5."

Christian Cipollini, BetMGM NFL trader: "A story of two different teams. There were some question marks around both the Bills and Chargers with new coaching, but it's gone in opposite directions. This certainly wasn't Bills -7 in the preseason. We're writing a lot more Bills action than Chargers, and I anticipate that to continue. That line has moved off how both teams have looked so far."

New England Patriots at Jacksonville Jaguars

Feazel: "Obviously Patriots were a disappointment in Week 1. Jaguars looked really efficient in Week 1 and fell to Broncos in Week 2. I don't think people have been super impressed with the Patriots so far, right now we're seeing more action on Jacksonville at home. We opened -2.5 on the Jags, now up to 3. Total at 45 and has stayed there. I'd expect more money on Jacksonville as we approach kickoff, maybe a little bit more two-way. Need will probably be Patriots and the under."

Cipollini: "Patriots have looked a little flat. Looking at the numbers we have now, if you're a Jags backer, you'll take 'em -3, and a Pats backer, you'll take them on ML. I expect kind of close to 50-50 action overall. We'll probably want Jags to win, but not cover."

Seattle Seahawks at Washington Commanders

Feazel: "Not a lot of Marcus Mariota fans apparently. The story for Seattle the first two weeks is that the defense is still a force. There was still some Cardinals love from Week 1, as the Week 2 game closed Seattle -3.5 in some spots. I'd anticipate Sam Darnold probably not to play in this one, as they haven't needed him to get these wins. Jadarian Price also questionable. One-way action on Seattle in this one."

Cipollini: "This line certainly wasn't 7 either, going into the season. Obviously off Jayden Daniels, we had him worth 4.5-5 points on the spread. I expect majority of action to be on the Seahawks, even though Washington is at home. If we do end up getting Darnold, it won't move much maybe to 7.5. If it does end up being Drew Lock, I could see getting a little more mixed action."

Baltimore Ravens at Dallas Cowboys (in Brazil)

Feazel: "Still seeing more money on the Ravens at this point. Will be interested to see how the field impacts this game, but it's still the highest total on the board. We'll see how the field conditions are as we get closer to that game. We saw this impacting the running side of the game, which would impact Ravens more. We opened Ravens -3.5 (-105), and we're still at -3.5. It'll be interesting to see line movement closer as we get more info on field conditions."

Cipollini: "Of the non prime-time games, this is the one I'd expect we'll take the most handle on. Highest point total of the week. Both defenses have looked pretty shaky and two good offenses going at it. Similar to Jags-Patriots, Ravens are 3.5-point favorites, I expect closer to 50-50 action. Plenty of fans on both sides, we'll get good two-way action. There's still so much unknown regarding the field conditions. I do think that the total was going to be inflated a little because of that, but too much unknown and nothing to really quantify. We'll reassess after."

Los Angeles Rams at Denver Broncos

Feazel: "We saw all the love for the Rams this offseason, and then they lost in Week 1. We actually needed the Rams on Monday night and they got there against the Giants. A little bit more money on the Rams right now, but expecting two-way action. Rams certainly looked more efficient on offense than in Australia; maybe it was the travel or the 49ers are really good. I don't see this getting to Rams -3 or down to -1.5, I think -2.5 should be the number. Total down from 46.5 to 45.5, money leaning more towards the under."

Cipollini: "We expect a ton of handle for this one, it should be a really good matchup. Rams still below that field goal number, I'll be curious to see where this ends up – I think it'll go to Rams -3. If I had to guess it'll be 60-40 Rams action. Anytime it's a prime-time game, we'll be rooting for a low-scoring game. We tend to get four times as much action on these games than on the 1 p.m. ET games."

item.title: Cowboys interested in trade for Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr.
item.description: The Cowboys are back in some trade rumors
item.content:encoded:
The Dallas Cowboys see their window of opportunity to make a Super Bowl run as right now. Owner and general manager Jerry Jones hasn’t been shy about making a move to improve his team, and he may already be laying the groundwork for a potential in-season trade.

NFL Insider Adam Schefter says the Cowboys, along with a handful of other teams, have inquired about trading for Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. Schefter also says that the Steelers are willing to listen to offers, but wouldn’t deal their cornerback unless they got a strong compensation package in return.

The Cowboys front office hasn’t been shy about making deals with the Steelers. They traded for George Pickens last year and acquired Broderick Jones before this season started. The team is also becoming very thin in the secondary with Cobie Durant out for a few weeks with a hamstring injury and P.J. Locke going on injured reserve.

Dallas also wants to give Christian Parker every tool he can for success, so a move for Porter Jr. would give him a prototypical, high-ceiling cornerback who could fit the scheme.

If Dallas is serious about going after a player like Porter Jr., it will truly be an all-in move with their sights set on a championship run.

item.title: NFL odds, betting, storylines: 2 underdogs to back in Week 3
item.description: Let's look at two spots where some 'dogs are in position to bark.
item.content:encoded:
If you're a fan of betting home underdogs in the NFL, Week 3 offers a cornucopia of options. More than half of this week's home teams — nine of 16 — are catching points.

Problem is, home underdogs haven't exactly been barking so far. Through two weeks, they have posted one victory and covered three point spreads in eight opportunities.

Is that script about to flip? Perhaps. Let's breakdown two NFL underdog best bets for Week 3.

Texas (-3) at Colts

How can I justify betting on a franchise that has lost nine straight games? One that has covered the spread just three times during this slump (including zero times in four games on its own turf)? One that has lost five straight times to the same division rival it is hosting this week?

It isn't easy. But hear me out: First, the Colts have opened the season against two Super Bowl contenders (Baltimore and Kansas City). And they showed a lot of fight in both games.

Yes, Indianapolis dug itself a 28-6 hole in the opener against the Ravens. However, from there, it outscored Baltimore 17-13. Then, last Sunday night in Kansas City, the Colts had the Chiefs on the ropes for more than 60 minutes, eventually succumbing 33-30 in overtime as a 6-point underdog.

Admittedly, quarterback Daniel Jones has looked so-so in his first two games back from his Achilles injury (41-for-62, 376 yards, two TDs, two INTs). But his right-hand man — running back Jonathan Taylor — has been outstanding (253 scrimmage yards, four rushing touchdowns).

Will Jones and the offense miss top wide receiver Alec Pierce (likely out multiple weeks with a heel injury)? Absolutely. Does the defense need to play better? For sure. But I don't trust this Texans team that dropped its first two games at home while surrendering 56 points, committing four turnovers and forcing zero.

In particular, I don't trust C.J. Stroud, who has just two TD passes to show for his 627 passing yards. Houston's quarterback also has been sacked 13 times in his last four games and thrown seven interceptions in his last three road contests (including the playoffs). 

Finally, for what it's worth, Indy hasn't opened a season 0-3 since 2021, nor started 0-3 ATS since 2015.

Bet: Colts +3

Cardinals at 49ers (-8.5)

There's no sugarcoating Arizona's second-half performance in last week's 31-7 home loss to Seattle. After scoring a game-tying touchdown with 3 seconds to play in the opening half, the Cardinals got steamrolled 24-0 over the final 30 minutes.

So what makes me confident that Arizona — which entered the season projected to be an NFL bottom-feeder — can go on the road and compete against a 49ers outfit that has looked flat-out dominant? 

Well, for one thing, the Cardinals' defense played terrific through the first six quarters of 2026. Before last week's second-half collapse, it yielded just three total touchdowns and 394 combined yards to the Chargers and Seahawks.

Also, Arizona has fared well against the 49ers from a betting perspective the past two years, covering in three of four meetings. That includes a 24-23 upset in San Francisco as a 7.5-point underdog in Week 5 of the 2024 season. And if you want to go back a decade, the Cardinals are 7-2-1 ATS at Levi's Stadium.

Of perhaps more relevance is the fact that this is a potential combination letdown/trap game for the 49ers. After waxing the unprepared Rams 27-7 in Australia and obliterating the god-awful Dolphins 35-13 at home last week, San Francisco follows this contest with back-to-back games against Denver (home) and archrival Seattle (road).  

Given what lies ahead, the 49ers might not be entirely focused for 60 minutes Sunday against a second straight vastly inferior opponent — an opponent that already caught one team napping this season.

Bet: Cardinals +8.5

LAST WEEK: 2-1

SEASON: 2-4

item.title: NFL betting, odds, lines: Betting trends to know for Week 3's biggest games
item.description: Here are a few betting trends to help you with your wagers in Week 3.
item.content:encoded:
NFL favorites took care of business during the opening week of the 2026 season, winning 12 of 16 games. They also posted a slightly profitable 9-7 ATS mark.

Not much changed in Week 2. Although there were three shocking upsets — the Ravens, Buccaneers and Chargers all lost as substantial favorites at home — favorites still finished 11-5 SU and 8-8 ATS.

Which brings us to an interesting NFL betting trends narrative that is present on the Week 3 oddsboard: Road teams are favored in nine of 16 games, with five of those visitors laying more than a field goal.

How have road favorites fared so far in the young season? 7-1 SU, 5-3 ATS.

Sticking with the prevailing Week 3 theme, my latest NFL betting trends breakdown features four road favorites among five of this week's marquee matchups.

New England Patriots at Jacksonville Jaguars (-3, 45.5)

Moneyline: Patriots +130/Jaguars -155

• The Patriots are one of just eight teams off to a 2-0 ATS start. After covering the closing 3.5-point spread in a season-opening loss at Seattle, New England throttled the visiting Steelers 20-3 as a 4.5-point home chalk in Week 2.

The last time the Patriots had a three-game point spread winning streak to begin a season: 2016. New England is 4-5 SU and 2-7 ATS in Week 3 since 2017.

• Jacksonville's nine-game SU and ATS winning streak ended in Denver in Week 2. After building a 13-3 third-quarter lead, the Jaguars surrendered 17 unanswered points to fall 20-13 as a 2.5-point underdog.

As they return to Florida, though, the Jaguars have this positive NFL betting trend working in their favor: They're 9-1 SU and ATS in their last 10 regular-season home games, with six double-digit blowouts.

• Including the narrow spread-cover at Seattle, the Patriots are 6-2 ATS in their last eight regular season contests as an underdog with five outright upsets.

Also, much like Jacksonville has been dominant at home, the Pats have been road warriors of late, going 8-2 SU and 9-1 ATS in their last 10 as a visitor.

• The Jaguars' defense is yielding an average of just 14.6 points per game over the last 10 regular-season games, while holding nine opponents to less than 21 points.

The Patriots' stop unit has been just as stout, allowing 36 total points over the last four regular-season games and limiting 15 of its last 20 regular-season opponents to 21 points or fewer.

That being said, the over is 4-0 in Jacksonville's last four at home and 4-2 in New England's last six on the highway.

Minnesota Vikings (-1.5, 42.5) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Moneyline: Vikings -120/Buccaneers +105

• Minnesota ran its winning streak to seven with last week's 9-3 victory in soggy Chicago as a 4.5-point underdog.

The Vikings, who are one of eight remaining unbeaten teams, are 6-0-1 ATS during their heater (3-0 ATS on the road and 3-0-1 ATS as a favorite).

• A week after tallying 59 points at Carolina, the Bears mustered just a single field goal against Minnesota's defense. 

That defense is now yielding an average of exactly 11 points during the seven-game winning streak, with only two opponents tallying more than 13 points.

• Tampa Bay endured one of the NFL's biggest upsets of the young season in Week 2, falling to the Browns 23-19 as an 8.5-point home favorite — the same Browns team that got whacked 34-10 in Week 1.

Bet the Minnesota Vikings to cover the spread at sportsbooks

The Buccaneers have now failed to cover the point spread in 11 consecutive games. They're also 0-2 SU and ATS for the first time since 2014, when they dropped their first three games on the scoreboard and at the betting window.

• Two other dubious NFL betting trends working against Tampa Bay: Since 2021, the team is 1-4 SU and 0-5 ATS in Week 3. The Bucs are 0-4 SU and ATS in their last four games as an underdog.

• Since Week 17 of the 2024 campaign, the over is 8-2 in games at Raymond James Stadium.

Conversely, the under has hit in four of Minnesota's last five road outings. The Vikings and their opponents failed to top 29 points in any of the four contests that fell short of the total.

Baltimore Ravens (-3, 52.5) at Dallas Cowboys in Brazil

Moneyline: Ravens -180/Cowboys +150

• Like the Bucs, Baltimore was stunned as an 8.5-point home favorite in Week 2, falling 24-17 to the Saints.

One week after racking up 506 yards and 41 points (on five touchdowns) at Indianapolis, the Ravens managed just 312 yards and two TDs.

• Dallas bounced back from a 28-20 opening loss at the Giants with a 37-20 Week 2 blowout of Washington, easily cashing as a 4.5-point home favorite.

It was the first time since a 31-28 upset of Kansas City on Thanksgiving Day (Week 13) that the Cowboys covered the point spread. On the bright side, Dallas is 5-0 ATS (3-1-1 SU) in its last five as a home underdog.

• Baltimore hits the road looking to improve on this solid NFL betting trend: It is 6-1 SU and ATS in its last seven as a visitor.

In the six victories, the Ravens outscored their opponents by an average of 16 points (30.7-14.7). 

• Cowboys QB Dak Prescott had four touchdowns last week against the Commanders. Not including games he departed injured, Prescott has tossed multiple TDs in 26 of his last 36 contests (including 14 of 18 at home).

This week, he faces a Baltimore secondary that has permitted multiple passing TDs just once in the last seven games.

• The over is 15-5 in the Ravens' last 20 road games (playoffs included). Nine of those contests cleared 52 combined points, including a 28-25 victory at Dallas in Week 3 of 2024.

Also, the Cowboys' first two games of 2026 have soared past the total. The over is now 20-6-1 in the Cowboys' last 27 games (7-0-1 in the last eight), including 9-4-1 in Dallas.

During this stretch, the Cowboys and their opponents have hurdled 52 points a dozen times.

Los Angeles Rams (-2.5, 45.5) at Denver Broncos

Moneyline: Rams -145/Broncos +120

• The Rams shook off the effects of an uninspiring 27-7 Week 1 loss to San Francisco in Australia with a Monday Night Football rout of the Giants by a near-identical score (28-6).

With its resounding victory as a 6.5-point home favorite, Los Angeles improved to 22-9 SU and 21-10 ATS in its last 31 regular-season games. 

During this stretch, the Rams are 9-4 SU and 10-3 ATS in true road games, and 8-2 SU and ATS as a road favorite.

• Denver followed an ugly 31-10 season-opening loss at Kansas City by rallying from a 13-3 halftime deficit to knock off Jacksonville 20-13 as a 2.5-point home favorite.

The Broncos have now won 14 of their last 16 regular season games, but are only 7-8-1 ATS. 

• Denver also is 14-1 SU in its last 15 regular-season contests in the Mile High City, but only 5-4-1 ATS since the start of last season. However, two of those point spread triumphs were outright upsets as a home underdog. 

In fact, the Broncos are 4-1 SU and ATS in their last five when catching points (the only setback coming in Week 1 at Kansas City).

• Denver has held three of its last four regular season opponents to 13 points or fewer, and 10 of its last 16 foes to less than 20 points.

Meanwhile, Los Angeles has tallied at least 28 points in 10 of its last 13 contests (including four of five on the road).

• Both the Rams and Broncos have stayed under the total in each of their first two games.

However, the over cashed in seven of L.A.'s eight true road contests last year (including the last five in a row). All seven topped 50 combined points.

Philadelphia Eagles (-4.5, 41.5) at Chicago Bears

Moneyline: Eagles -225/Bears +185

• Philadelphia kicked off 2026 with a pair of narrow victories, following a 24-22 home win over the Commanders with a last-minute 24-20 comeback triumph at the Titans in Week 2.

The Eagles failed to cover the spread as a six-point favorite vs. Washington and seven-point chalk at Tennessee), and are now in an 0-4 ATS funk dating to last season (playoffs included).

Philly hasn't begun a season with three straight non-covers since 2020.

• After compiling eight touchdowns and 552 yards in their jaw-dropping 59-37 victory Week 1 at Carolina, the Bears returned home and managed just one field goal and 297 yards in a lackluster 9-3 home loss to Minnesota as a 4.5-point favorite.

Despite that setback, Chicago remains 13-6 SU and 14-4-1 ATS (playoffs included) since starting last year 0-2 SU and ATS.

Over this 19-game period, the Bears are 7-3 SU and ATS at home, and 6-4 SU and 8-1-1 ATS as an underdog (including a 24-15 upset of the Eagles as a 7-point road underdog in Week 13 last season).

Bet under 41.5 total points in Bears-Eagles at sportsbooks now

• Here's are several impressive multi-year NFL betting trends involving the Eagles:

They started 4-0 or better three times in the past four seasons. Philly was 4-0 in 2025, 5-0 in 2023 and 8-0 in 2022. And while they split their first two contests in 2024, the Eagles then embarked on a 10-game winning streak.

What's more, Philadelphia opened up 7-3 ATS last year, 8-4 ATS in 2024, 8-2-1 ATS in 2023 and 5-2 ATS in 2022. The team's Week 3 mark over this four-year span: 4-0 SU and ATS.

• The under is 6-1-1 in the last eight games played at Soldier Field. Five of those contests fell short of 42 combined points.
