item.content:encoded:
Update 9/27: Williams has a Grade 2 hamstring strain, and is expected to miss 3-4 weeks, according to ESPN. He is out for Chicago’s Monday Night game against the Philadelphia Eagles, and is slated to miss the following two games against the New York Jets and Green Bay Packers. The Bears face the Atlanta Falcons in Week 6, then play on Thursday Night Football in Week 7 against the New England Patriots — two possible options for Williams’ return. Chicago’s backup QB Tyson Bagent has been in concussion protocol. Either Bagent or Case Keenum will start for the Bears in Week 3 against the Eagles.

Update Monday afternoon: Williams “avoided any major injury to his hamstring,” according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero. He hasn’t been ruled out for Week 3 against the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night yet. This seems like the best case scenario for the Bears. Ben Johnson called the injury “week to week.”

Update: Williams will have an MRI on Monday to determine the severity of his hamstring injury, per Adam Schefter.

Caleb Williams looked like a potential MVP candidate during Week 1, as he led a Chicago Bears offense that hung 59 points on the board against the Carolina Panthers.

But the combination of weather in Chicago — and a Brian Flores-led Minnesota Vikings defense — has made for tougher sledding in Week 2.

And now the Bears quarterback could be dealing with a lower-body injury.

Williams had to be helped off the field after a short run midway through the fourth quarter, and the injury brought backup quarterback Tyson Bagent into the game.

You can see the moment here, as it appears Williams goes down with a non-contact injury:

The only sound you could hear after the play was Williams crying out in pain, as the Bears-heavy crowd at Soldier Field was stunned into silence. Williams as helped off the field, as Bagent entered the game.

Making matters worse, Chicago’s possession stalled and a potential game-tying field goal was blocked, just as Williams was being taken to the locker room on a cart:

Now we wait on word regarding Chicago’s star quarterback.

Update: The team is calling this a hamstring injury:

This is a developing story and will be updated.

item.title: Week 3 NFL odds, picks, predictions: Our best bets for the weekend's games
item.description: Our NFL handicappers give out their favorite bets for Week 3 games.
item.content:encoded:
Week 3 of the NFL season began with a dominating 35-14 Atlanta Falcons victory over the Green Bay Packers in Green Bay's home opener at Lambeau Field.

What will the rest of the weekend have in store for bettors?

Our NFL handicapping team of Matt Jacob, Jeremy Pond and Matt Russell combine to give their best bets for Week 3 of the NFL season.

Odds subject to change.

Los Angeles Chargers at Buffalo Bills (-7, 50.5)

Jacob: Through eight quarters — all played on their home turf — the Chargers' offense has produced four touchdowns. Against two teams (Arizona and Las Vegas) that each finished 3-14 a year ago while ranking 28th (Cardinals) and 25th (Raiders) in scoring defense.

Bills quarterback Josh Allen? He accounted for five touchdowns (three passing, two rushing) last week! This after tallying four scores in Week 1 at Houston. In fact, in their 41-31 Week 2 win over Detroit, the Bills scored nearly as many first-half points (27) as the Chargers have scored in two games (28). 

Lest you think I've come to only bury Justin Herbert and the Chargers' Mike McDaniels-crafted offense, fear not: Through eight quarters, the defense has surrendered 52 points (26 in each game) to a pair of opponents that ranked 32nd (Raiders) and 23rd (Cardinals) in scoring offense in 2025.

Bet the Buffalo Bills to cover the spread at sportsbooks right now

Now, after getting embarrassed as a substantial home favorite the last two weeks, the Chargers travel to the other side of the country. For a game that kicks at 10 a.m. PT. Against a 2-0 Bills squad that has tallied 77 points, had 10 days off and is in the midst of a three-game homestand.

Look, this isn't a sophisticated handicap, because it doesn't need to be. Unless I'm falling into a massive trap — and maybe I am — this point spread makes zero sense. By the way, the Chargers' point spread record last season in early East Coast games? 0-4.

Bet: Bills -7

Russell: I showed up to put in THE WINDOW's free best bet into this file and, lo and behold, there was already one on this game. It just happens to be on the opposite side. So, we'll play a little devil's advocate here.

Jacob's right about (waves hands wildly) all of it on the Chargers side of things, but this is the best example of the necessary reminder in Week 3 that we've only actually played two games per team. If this was the NBA or NHL, we wouldn't blink about two bad games.

As much as I'm also tempted to brand L.A. with the scarlet 'B' for "bad," it's the basics that led to the Chargers getting upset. However, this is more about the perception of the Bills relative to where it was just two weeks ago. 

Here's what we knew before Week 1:

  • Josh Allen is awesome, and the Bills offense won't skip a beat with Joe Brady promoted to head coach.

  • There's going to be some growing pains for the defense in a shift in personnel and scheme.

Both things have remained true. 

We now know two other things before Week 3:

  • The Bills were a dropped-interception in Week 1 from starting 0-1

  • The market moved against their Week 2 opponent because of how much of a rest advantage the Bills had, and how thin the Lions' secondary is to start the season. 

Yet, before the Rams' bounce-back win on Monday night, the Bills were power-rated as the best team in the NFL in the betting market. 

Bet the Los Angeles Chargers to cover the spread at sportsbooks right now

For all the trends against the Chargers, the most relevant one is the situation L.A. finds themselves in: Since 2003, NFL teams starting 0-2 have gone 107-85-5 ATS (55.7%) in Week 3. Whether that's due to the qualitative assessment of the winless team's "desperation" or the quantitative understanding that the Bills' market rating has increased significantly through two games, all while the Chargers have hit their perceived floor, you can understand why there's value on L.A. at a full touchdown. 

If the Chargers can clean up the basics — fumbles, blocked punts, penalties to star offensive linemen — there's not a big talent gap between the two sides, which is why this game was lined at Bills -2.5 this summer.

Bet: Chargers +7

Pond: While my colleagues are thumb wrestling over which side will cover the spread, I am digging into the player props ahead of this showdown.

And the angles I'm targeting are specifically tied to one player.

Only five pass-catchers have more than 200 yards receiving so far this season. That elite group includes four wide receivers: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (277 yards), Chris Olave (268), Davante Adams (221) and Amon-Ra St. Brown (209). The player currently ranked third in the quintet — and only tight end on the list — is Dalton Kincaid.

Finally healthy, the Buffalo tight end has been on fire to start the campaign. He has 12 catches on 14 targets for 225 yards and a touchdown for the Bills (2-0), and I think he maintains that hot pace.

The Chargers, who have opened with eerie, back-to-back 26-14 defeats to the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders, can't seem to stop anyone. Jacoby Brissett and Kirk Cousins combined for 530 yards and four touchdowns in the air against Los Angeles.

Now, the Chargers face Allen, the early NFL MVP favorite, who should be able to pick apart that porous defense and consistently find Kincaid. Through the first two games, Kincaid leads the Bills in routes, catches, targets and yards. I don't see those trends stopping here.

I'm backing Kincaid to clear 4.5 receptions for the third consecutive time and score in a game where I think Allen will find plenty of success getting the ball downfield.

Bets: TE Dalton Kincaid over 4.5 receptions (+106, FanDuel) and anytime TD (+198, Caesars)

New York Jets at Detroit Lions (-6.5, 47.5)

Jacob: During a stellar 15-year career playing defensive back for five different teams, Aaron Glenn snagged 41 interceptions across 205 games. Through his first 19 games as head coach of the New York Jets, where he played eight of his 15 seasons, Glenn has seen his defense collect exactly — hang on, grabbing my calculator — zero interceptions.

Remarkable as it is to believe, the Jets' defense hasn't secured an INT since picking off the mighty Tyler Huntley twice in the 2024 season finale. The 19-game drought is the longest in NFL history. And get this: It covers 576 pass attempts.

Is there any reason to believe New York's INT slump will end this week? In a word, nope. Lions quarterback Jared Goff has put the ball in the air 77 times already this season, and not once has he completed a pass to the wrong team. In fact, Goff has been picked off in just 10 of his last 33 starts overall.

Yes, this wager is a bit "juicy," but for good reason.

Bet: Jared Goff under 0.5 interceptions (-145)

Seattle Seahawks (-7.5, 40.5) at Washington Commanders

Pond: When Sam Darnold went down on opening night, I thought for sure his absence would have major ramifications for the Seattle offense and wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

Well, little did we know that backup quarterback Drew Lock was ready to play like an All Pro as his replacement. The seven-year veteran has been playing at an elite level for the Seahawks (2-0), completing 35-of-48 passes for 422 yards and four touchdowns with no interceptions.

And the greatest benefactor of his stellar play has been Smith-Njigba. The NFL's top pass-catcher has 22 receptions for those aforementioned league-best 277 yards and four touchdowns. He was unstoppable in Seattle's 31-7 rout of the Arizona Cardinals, hauling in nine passes on 11 targets from Lock and three touchdowns.

Now, he's likely going to be matched up against Mike Sainristil, who is off to a terrible start to the season. The Washington cornerback has given up six receptions on eight targets (75%) so far this season.

Needless to say, it's going to be a long day for Sainristil and the Washington secondary trying to cover Smith-Njigba.

I am also throwing in Seattle tight end AJ Barner to score anytime.

We're getting a good price on a guy facing a winless franchise that gave up a combined eight catches for 120 yards and four touchdowns to tight ends Dallas Goedert and Jake Ferguson in its first two games.

Expect big games from Barner and Smith-Njigba in this affair.

Bets: WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba Parlay: 60+ yards receiving, 7+ receptions and anytime TD (+219, FanDuel) and TE AJ Barner anytime (+320, FanDuel)

Las Vegas Raiders at New Orleans Saints (-3, 43.5)

Pond: Juwan Johnson has clearly solidified himself as one of QB Tyler Shough's favorite targets not named Chris Olave, making seven catches on 11 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown in the first two games.

If we look deeper into the data, the numbers look even better for Johnson when Shough is taking the snaps. The duo has connected on 48 receptions for 641 yards and three touchdowns in the 11 games Shough has been the New Orleans starter.

Add that all together and I think we're getting an absolute steal here with this number. Johnson has had four or more receptions in a whopping 14 of his last 19 games (82 percent) across the last two seasons, giving me a lot of confidence he will clear this number again.

Bet: TE Juwan Johnson over 3.5 receptions (-102, FanDuel)

Los Angeles Rams (-2.5, 44.5) at Denver Broncos

Pond: Welcome home, Terrance Ferguson.

The second-year tight end makes his return to the state of Colorado in this marquee Sunday Night Football matchup at Mile High Stadium. And if the native of Littleton, Colo., puts together an effort similar to his Week 2 showing, Denver is going to be in trouble.

With Puka Nacua a late scratch in Monday night's game against the New York Giants, it was Ferguson who Matthew Stafford targeted as his second option to Davante Adams in the 28-6 victory. Ferguson finished with six catches for 54 yards and a touchdown after putting up zeros in the season opener against San Francisco in Australia.

Reports have Nacua likely missing this showdown with Denver, which means we should see a heavy dose of Ferguson in this explosive Los Angeles offense.

Back the Heritage (Colo.) High School product to hit pay dirt for the second consecutive game on "home" soil.

Bet: TE Terrance Ferguson anytime touchdown (+200, Caesars)

item.title: Panthers are expected to have Jalen Coker Sunday
item.description: A pair of Panthers wide receivers carry questionable tags into Sunday's game in Cleveland and it looks like at least one of them will be able to play.
item.content:encoded:
A pair of Panthers wide receivers carry questionable tags into Sunday's game in Cleveland and it looks like at least one of them will be able to play.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Jalen Coker is expected to play. Coker has been dealing with an ankle injury for the last couple of weeks and was limited in practice on Friday.

Xavier Legette was also limited on Friday after missing Thursday's practice with a knee injury that popped up during the week. He is viewed as a game-time decision for the 1-1 Panthers.

The wideouts are the only questionable players for Carolina. Linebacker Devin Lloyd and safety Nick Scott have been ruled out.

item.title: Justin Fields could be returning to New York
item.description: Woody Johnson's favorite quarterback could be returning to New York.
item.content:encoded:
Woody Johnson's favorite quarterback could be returning to New York.

Justin Fields, who was traded by the Jets to the Chiefs as part of the plan to have a capable replacement in the event Patrick Mahomes wasn't ready for Week 1, has emerged as an option for the Giants, who have made it clear they will look at all options.

Fields has been mentioned multiple times in recent days by multiple reporters, which means that the word is out that Fields could be a possibility for the Giants.

The Giants are expected to make a move as soon as Monday. Jameis Winston's performance against the Titans on Sunday will surely be a factor in the question of whether they're looking for someone to serve as Winston's backup — or someone who could eventually supplant him while starter Jaxson Dart misses at least the balance of the regular season after knee surgery.

The two-year, $40 million contract Fields signed last year with the Jets included $10 million guaranteed for 2026. The Chiefs are paying him $3 million, and the Jets are paying $7 million. With Mahomes looking like Mahomes again, the Chiefs could recoup their 2027 sixth-round pick and unload the balance of Fields's 2026 salary.

The Chiefs also would have to be willing to elevate rookie Garrett Nussmeier into the QB2 role behind Mahomes, unless coach Andy Reid and G.M. Brett Veach have someone else in mind who could be the backup to Mahomes.

Giants coach John Harbaugh has limited experience against Fields. In 2021, Fields (then a rookie with the Bears), started a Week 11 game against the Ravens. He left with a rib injury after completing four of 11 passes for 79 yards and rushing one time for four yards. During his single season with the Steelers, Fields played three snaps in a Week 11 game against the Ravens that Russell Wilson started. Fields ran the ball twice for 17 yards. In the wild-card game that same year between the Steelers and Ravens, Fields played two snaps, throwing one pass that did not connect.

Still, Fields apparently is on the radar screen for a return to New York, where the other team that plays in MetLife Stadium will be paying him a lot more than whatever the Giants would contribute to his 2026 W-2.
